briefs.title: artifact content endpoint parity testing
briefs.description: Use artifact content endpoint parity testing to compare raw SKILL.md with its ZIP entry, assert byte equality, and catch shared builder regressions.
briefs.coreQuestion: How do you prove SKILL.md inside the ZIP is byte-for-byte equivalent to the raw content endpoint for the same database row?

outline.heading: What Must Artifact Content Endpoint Parity Testing Prove?
outline.coverage: Define parity as identical UTF-8 bytes produced from one skill row, while separating markdown parity from ZIP container checksum behavior.

outline.heading: How Does a ZIP Raw Markdown Parity Test Work?
outline.coverage: Trace the artifact route through buildSkillMarkdown, JSZip generation, archive extraction, and comparison with the content route response.

outline.heading: How Should a SKILL.md Byte Equality Assertion Be Written?
outline.coverage: Compare Buffer values rather than normalized strings so line endings, trailing newlines, frontmatter order, and encoding changes remain visible.

outline.heading: Artifact Content Contract Testing Across Response Types
outline.coverage: Cover content types, archive paths, response status, requested version behavior, and the canonical markdown payload without conflating transport metadata.

outline.heading: How Do You Verify Two Download Endpoints Consistency?
outline.coverage: Use one seeded row and request by both UUID and slug, then prove each route selects the same row and returns the same generated SKILL.md.

outline.heading: Detecting a Shared Markdown Builder Regression
outline.coverage: Mutate array fields, defaults, optional GitHub metadata, and fallback body content to expose drift in the common serialization helper.

outline.heading: Parity Matrix for IDs, Versions, and Markdown Fields
outline.coverage: Present the required table for UUID and slug lookups, matching and mismatched versions, optional fields, and expected byte-level outcomes.

outline.heading: How Do You Run the Endpoint Parity Procedure?
outline.coverage: Turn the procedure plan into an integration test that seeds once, calls both handlers, extracts the archive entry, and emits a useful first-difference diagnostic.

outline.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
outline.coverage: Answer five to eight concise questions about ZIP metadata, line endings, UUID lookup, version mismatches, hashing, and binary versus string comparison.

outline.heading: Conclusion
outline.coverage: Summarize the single-builder contract and direct readers to the verified skill catalog CTA.

tablePlan.title: Artifact and content endpoint parity matrix

procedurePlan.heading: How to prove byte parity
steps: Seed one deterministic skill row with every markdown field represented.
Call the raw content handler by slug and capture its response as a Buffer.
Call the artifact handler for the same slug and current version.
Load the returned ZIP and extract the exact <slug>/SKILL.md entry as bytes.
Assert Buffer equality and report the first differing byte and nearby text.
Repeat with UUID lookup, optional fields, and the fallback body branch.

briefs.title: install telemetry replay protection testing
briefs.description: Use install telemetry replay protection testing to expose duplicate events, retry-driven counter inflation, and missing idempotency controls.
briefs.coreQuestion: How do you prove retries or replayed install requests do not create duplicate events and inflate counters when no idempotency key is stored?

outline.heading: What Does Install Telemetry Replay Protection Testing Expose?
outline.coverage: Explain the current append-and-increment flow, why POST retries can repeat side effects, and which observable outcomes define a replay defect.

outline.heading: How Should Duplicate Install Event Prevention Be Tested?
outline.coverage: Send identical normalized add events concurrently and sequentially, then compare install rows and both counters with a one-event oracle.

outline.heading: What Belongs in a Telemetry Idempotency Key Test?
outline.coverage: Define stable key scope, payload binding, retention, response replay, and conflicting reuse cases without claiming the current route already stores a key.

outline.heading: Retry Counter Inflation QA Matrix
outline.coverage: Model client timeout, gateway retry, double click, concurrent delivery, and delayed replay against installCount and weeklyInstalls.

outline.heading: How Do You Run Replayed POST Request Testing?
outline.coverage: Capture one valid body and send controlled copies while recording request identity, row count, counter deltas, and response semantics.

outline.heading: Install Event Deduplication Design Options
outline.coverage: Compare a unique event ID, idempotency table, conditional insert, and transactional counter update using the current schema as the baseline.

outline.heading: Replay Fixtures and Expected Database Deltas
outline.coverage: Use the required table to distinguish the current behavior from the target once-only side-effect contract.

outline.heading: How Do You Add Replay Tests to CI?
outline.coverage: Provide an ordered integration workflow with isolated skill counters, deterministic event keys, parallel requests, and database cleanup.

outline.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
outline.coverage: Answer questions about HTTP idempotency, retry ownership, remove and update events, deduplication windows, concurrency, and unknown skills.

outline.heading: Conclusion
outline.coverage: State the measurable once-only contract and point to the skill directory CTA.

tablePlan.title: Install replay scenario and side-effect matrix

procedurePlan.heading: How to test replay protection
steps: Create a skill fixture with zero install and weekly counters.
Record the installs row count and both counter values.
Send one add payload twice with the same proposed idempotency key.
Repeat the pair concurrently to expose race behavior.
Assert one accepted event row and a counter delta of one for the target contract.
Repeat for remove, update, conflicting payload, and unknown-skill cases.

briefs.title: install telemetry reference resolution testing
briefs.description: Use install telemetry reference resolution testing to verify UUID, slug, and display-name lookup order, exact matches, and safe unknown references.
briefs.coreQuestion: How do you prove install telemetry resolves canonical UUIDs directly, then tries exact slug, then exact display name?

outline.heading: What Must Install Telemetry Reference Resolution Testing Prove?
outline.coverage: Define the accepted reference shapes and the exact UUID, slug, display-name, and unknown-reference outcomes exposed by the route.

outline.heading: How Does Telemetry UUID Slug Name Lookup Work?
outline.coverage: Trace normalization, UUID recognition, direct assignment, slug query, and final display-name query in execution order.

outline.heading: What Makes a Good Skill Reference Fallback Test?
outline.coverage: Use fixtures whose UUID, slug, and name values are intentionally distinct, including a name that resembles another slug.

outline.heading: Install Resolution Precedence Test Matrix
outline.coverage: Cover valid and malformed UUIDs, exact and case-variant slugs, exact display names, collisions, blanks, and unknown references.

outline.heading: How Do You Assert an Exact Slug Telemetry Query?
outline.coverage: Mock or inspect the Drizzle predicate and prove no partial, normalized, or case-folded match is silently introduced.

outline.heading: Display Name Install Lookup and Collision Risks
outline.coverage: Explain first-row behavior, duplicate display-name risk, and why deterministic fixture design matters for route-level tests.

outline.heading: Reference Inputs, Queries, and Expected IDs
outline.coverage: Present the table that maps each body field and reference value to the query path, resolved ID, insert decision, and counter outcome.

outline.heading: How Do You Implement the Resolution Contract Test?
outline.coverage: Follow the numbered procedure from fixture creation through query spying, POST execution, row assertion, and counter verification.

outline.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
outline.coverage: Answer questions about UUID syntax, skillSlug precedence, exact matching, duplicate names, unknown skills, and backward compatibility.

outline.heading: Conclusion
outline.coverage: Summarize the ordered lookup contract and use the catalog CTA.

procedurePlan.heading: How to verify reference resolution
steps: Seed two skills with distinct UUIDs, slugs, and display names.
Create payload fixtures for each reference shape and one ambiguous-looking value.
Run normalizeInstallEvent and assert ref plus refIsUuid before route execution.
Call POST and record which Drizzle lookup executes.
Assert the inserted skillId and counter delta for every resolved reference.
Assert unknown references return success without an install row.

codeExamples.focus: Exercise skillSlug precedence, skillId fallback, trimming, and refIsUuid.

briefs.title: install telemetry action mapping testing
briefs.description: Use install telemetry action mapping testing to cover add, remove, update, unknown, and conflicting fields without inflating install counters.
briefs.coreQuestion: How do you test install, remove, update, unknown, and conflicting action fields without inflating install counters?

outline.heading: What Must Install Telemetry Action Mapping Testing Cover?
outline.coverage: Define normalization outcomes for current action values, legacy installType values, missing fields, unknown text, and conflicts.

outline.heading: How Do You Build an Install Remove Update Telemetry Test?
outline.coverage: Test each supported action through both the pure normalizer and the POST route, including row persistence and counter changes.

outline.heading: How Should Tests Cover Unknown Action Defaults Add Behavior?
outline.coverage: Show the initialized add value, identify the risk of typo-driven increments, and define the expected behavior without inventing a different contract.

outline.heading: Legacy installType Precedence Cases
outline.coverage: Map legacy remove and update fields against absent, matching, and conflicting current action values.

outline.heading: How Does Counter Inflation Action Mapping Occur?
outline.coverage: Prove only normalized add events execute the SQL increments and expose cases where malformed values normalize to add.

outline.heading: Telemetry Conflicting Fields Test Design
outline.coverage: Use pairwise cases for action and installType so remove precedence, update precedence, and default behavior stay explicit.

outline.heading: Action Inputs, Normalized Values, and Counter Deltas
outline.coverage: Present a table covering supported, missing, unknown, mixed-case, non-string, and conflicting action fields.

outline.heading: How Do You Implement the Action Mapping Procedure?
outline.coverage: Build table-driven Vitest cases for normalization, then a smaller route integration set for insert and counter side effects.

outline.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
outline.coverage: Answer questions about default add behavior, legacy compatibility, case sensitivity, conflicts, updates, and counter assertions.

outline.heading: Conclusion
outline.coverage: Restate the mapping oracle and direct readers to the verified QA skill catalog.

procedurePlan.heading: How to test action mapping
steps: Define a table of current action and legacy installType combinations.
Call normalizeInstallEvent for every row and assert the exact normalized type.
Seed a skill with known install counters.
POST representative add, remove, update, unknown, and conflict cases.
Assert every resolved event row stores its normalized installType.
Assert only add cases increment installCount and weeklyInstalls.

briefs.title: Typesense timestamp mapping contract tests
briefs.description: Use Typesense timestamp mapping contract tests to verify int64 dates become valid SkillSummary ISO strings and catch field-name or fallback drift.
briefs.coreQuestion: How do you test that an int64 Typesense createdAt field becomes the ISO date string expected by SkillSummary consumers?

outline.heading: What Must Typesense Timestamp Mapping Contract Tests Prove?
outline.coverage: Define the boundary between an int64 index field and the ISO string consumed by SkillSummary, including malformed and absent values.

outline.heading: How Should Typesense int64 Date Conversion Work?
outline.coverage: Compare seconds, milliseconds, numeric strings, and ISO strings against the declared schema and the mapping implementation.

outline.heading: What Is the Search Document Timestamp Contract?
outline.coverage: State the producer field type, mapper output type, valid date requirement, and consumer expectations without masking a number through a TypeScript cast.

outline.heading: CreatedAt Epoch Fallback Test Cases
outline.coverage: Cover missing fields, null, zero, invalid text, and the explicit Unix epoch fallback while distinguishing valid fallback from invalid conversion.

outline.heading: How Do Typesense Camel Snake Date Fields Interact?
outline.coverage: Test createdAt precedence over created_at and detect conflicting values so migration compatibility remains deterministic.

outline.heading: SkillSummary Date Mapping Test Design
outline.coverage: Use typed fixtures and runtime assertions for string type, parseability, expected instant, and sort behavior.

outline.heading: Timestamp Input and Expected ISO Output Matrix
outline.coverage: Present the table for int64 seconds, int64 milliseconds, aliases, missing values, and invalid values.

outline.heading: How Do You Implement the Mapping Contract Procedure?
outline.coverage: Stub the Typesense result, call searchSkills, and assert both the mapped date and untouched pagination and facet fields.

outline.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
outline.coverage: Answer questions about Typesense int64 units, ISO strings, epoch fallback, field aliases, TypeScript casts, and sorting.

outline.heading: Conclusion
outline.coverage: State the runtime date contract and point readers to relevant skills.

procedurePlan.heading: How to test Typesense date mapping
steps: Create one hit fixture for every timestamp representation and alias case.
Stub the Typesense search call with a single controlled hit.
Call searchSkills using fixed pagination parameters.
Assert createdAt is a string and Date.parse returns the expected instant.
Assert the explicit fallback for a missing date.
Add a failing case that exposes numeric values returned unchanged by a cast.
